short: Continuous F0 targets from articulation were prior work; MVF carrying voicing instead of a flag is new but unproven: the F0 RMSE gain uses different reference contours and naturalness is not better.
position: The paper [@csapo2019ultrasound] swaps one parametric vocoder for another (M06) and changes the excitation (M08) of ultrasound-to-speech synthesis: continuous F0 and maximum voiced frequency replace the voiced/unvoiced flag and F0. Interpolated F0 targets were already used from articulatory signals [@liu2016articulatory; @gonzalez2017evaluation; @taguchi2018articulatory], so M08 is standard; what is new is letting MVF, taken from the group's speech-synthesis vocoder, carry voicing in place of the binary flag, and nothing shows it helps. The headline 31 Hz against 65 Hz RMSE compares predictions with two different reference contours, and the listening test finds no significant difference. M12 is behind the best comparable work: 11 earlier studies tested listener intelligibility of speech synthesized from non-acoustic signals, among them EMA-driven synthesis with 30.1% listener WER [@taguchi2018articulatory]; this one rates naturalness only. The parametric vocoder (M06) matched the field in 2019 and was replaced by a neural vocoder in the same lineage within a year [@csapo2020waveglow].
